subject: Dual-rate lock & grace-period amendment for Q4 order form
messages:
From: Emma Cole <emma@brightcare.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dual-rate lock proposal and grace period for Q4 order form

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to share the commercial ask so we can see if Redwood can accommodate it on the Q4 order form. High level: BrightCare wants a dual-rate lock for the first 12 months (introductory blended rate for months 1–6, stepped rate months 7–12) plus a 90-day grace period on true-ups for the first annual reconciliation.

Key asks:
- Introductory rate: $0.012/token equivalent for months 1–6.
- Step-up: 2% increase months 7–12 (capped).
- Floor/Cap: floor at $0.010/token equivalent, ceiling at $0.018/token equivalent during the 12-month period.
- Grace: 90 days after quarter close to submit usage evidence and true up; no automatic penalties during grace window.

We understand this is non-standard. If Redwood can accept, procurement will loop in legal to do a quick review and then DocuSign. I've attached a short SOW for context (BrightCare_SOW_Q4.pdf).

Can you confirm feasibility and any contract language concerns?

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Cole
VP, Procurement
BrightCare Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dual-rate lock proposal and grace period for Q4 order form

Hi Emma — appreciate the clear summary. Short answer: yes, we can make a dual-rate lock work, but we need to tighten a couple of operational and legal points so we don't create open-ended exposure for Redwood. Proposed adjustments:

1) Grace period: we can accept a grace window, but ask that it be 60 days (not 90) for the standard order form; we can stretch to 90 days for the first year as a gesture, provided BrightCare agrees to provide usage export in the agreed CSV schema.

2) Step-up percentage: 3% step-up (instead of 2%) for months 7–12 to reflect indexing and billing ops.

3) Cap/floor: we can live with the floor you proposed, but we want the ceiling language to include an annualized cap tied to the published rate card + quantization band so the ceiling doesn't block us from applying necessary model upgrades.

4) True-up mechanics: include an explicit "true-up calculation example" in Exhibit B and require mutual sign-off on the first true-up calculation to avoid disputes.

I've attached an initial redline (RF_Orderform_0610_redline.docx) with inline edits to Exhibit B. Can Marissa and Karthik weigh in on the proposed legal language and whether 60/90 approach is reasonable? Emma — we'll prepare a sample calculation in the next email for transparency.

Next step: if you can confirm acceptance of 60-day operational grace (90-day one-time for year 1) and 3% step-up, we'll share an updated PDF version suitable for DocuSign.

Best,

Proposed clause (to add to Exhibit B - Pricing):
"Dual-Rate Lock and True-Up"
1) For the first 12 months following Effective Date, Customer shall be billed at the Introductory Rate for months 1–6 and the Step-Up Rate for months 7–12, as set forth on the Order Form.
2) True-up: Customer shall provide usage reports in the CSV schema within sixty (60) calendar days following the end of each billing quarter; Redwood shall have thirty (30) calendar days to review and provide any dispute to Customer. For the initial 12-month term only, the parties may mutually agree to extend the Customer submission window to ninety (90) calendar days.
3) Cap/Floor: The Introductory Rate shall not be lower than the Floor Rate and the Step-Up Rate shall not exceed the Ceiling Rate. The Ceiling Rate shall be expressed as the greater of (a) the published Rate Card plus the Quantization Band, or (b) the Ceiling Rate specified on the Order Form.
4) Remedies: Failure by Customer to submit required usage evidence within the agreed submission window shall result in a provisional billing at the Step-Up Rate; any adjustments after submission shall be reflected in the next invoice following mutual reconciliation.

Comments: keep language precise around submission schema and dispute window. Also add a sample calculation table to Exhibit B to illustrate how the true-up works (see Jordan's note).

Marissa

From: Emma Cole <emma@brightcare.com>

Cc: procurement@brightcare.com

Subject: Re: Dual-rate lock proposal and grace period for Q4 order form

Jordan/Marissa — thanks for the quick turn. The 60/90 split on the submission window is reasonable. We do want clarity on the "provisional billing" point — procurement's finance team is concerned that provisional billing at the Step-Up Rate could create cash-flow volatility if our reporting is delayed for legitimate reasons (e.g., SOC-2 attestation timing). Can you provide the sample calculation you mentioned and confirm there will be a backbill/credit rather than a penalty?

Example that procurement asked for (they want to see how a true-up would flow):
Quarter usage (tokens): 12,500,000
Introductory months in quarter: months 1–2
Billed during quarter at Intro Rate: 5,000,000 tokens x $0.012 = $60,000
Remaining usage billed at Step-Up Rate: 7,500,000 tokens x $0.01236 (3% step-up) = $92,700
Quarter provisional invoice total = $152,700

If final true-up shows Introductory eligibility was overstated by 1,500,000 tokens, the reconciliation would credit the customer: 1,500,000 x (Step-Up - Intro) = 1,500,000 x $0.00036 = $540 credit on next invoice.

If Redwood can confirm this mechanics (provisional invoice + post-submission credit rather than penalty) and include it in Exhibit B's sample calculation, procurement can take the redline to legal for signature.

Best,
Emma
VP, Procurement
BrightCare Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Cole <emma@brightcare.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dual-rate lock proposal and grace period for Q4 order form

Emma — thanks for the worked example, that's perfect. Confirming Redwood's operational approach:
1) Provisional billing at the Step-Up Rate is intended to avoid undercollection; any overcollection will be credited on the next invoice once usage evidence is accepted. No penalty or late fee will be assessed purely for late submission if the delay is within the agreed grace window or is caused by documented compliance processes (e.g., SOC-2 delays).

2) Example calculation (replicating your numbers):
- Quarter total tokens: 12,500,000
- Introductory-eligible tokens (actual): 3,500,000
- Billed at Intro Rate (0.012): 3,500,000 x $0.012 = $42,000
- Remaining at Step-Up Rate (0.01236): 9,000,000 x $0.01236 = $111,240
- Provisional invoice = $153,240
- If final eligibility reduces Intro-eligible by 1,500,000 -> credit = 1,500,000 x ($0.01236 - $0.012) = $540 credit applied to next invoice.

3) Operational note: we will require usage exports in the agreed CSV format and an S3 share link or secure upload for automated reconciliation.

I'll add this worked example to the redline and confirm with Finance that credits appear as line-item adjustments (not separate refunds). HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/BRIGHT-2026-413
